newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada parliament gets Canada-Israel trade pact.
newsitem.headline: Canada parliament gets Canada-Israel trade pact.

text.p: Canadian International Trade Minister Art Eggleton introduced legislation into Parliament on Thursday to implement the Canada-Israel Free Trade Agreement.
"The agreement will open doors for Canadian companies and ultimately increase exports and create jobs at home," Eggleton said in a statement.
"Once the agreement is implemented, Canadian exporters will be on an equal footing with their U.S. and European competitors, who now have the benefit of free trade agreements Hwith Israel."
On July 31 the two countries signed the agreement, whjich is to take effect at the start of 1997 if both sides complete the necessary legislation in time.

Eggleton's statement added that Canada intends to extend the same benefits to Palestinians that Israel will enjoy. It will conduct discussions with Palestinian officials to examine the next step in this process.
The agreement will remove industrial tariffs -- except on women's swimwear and certain cotton fabric.
Duty-free access or low duties will be applied to a variety of agricultural and fisheries products -- but excluding dairy, poultry and egg products.

Canada will get better access for its grains, grain products, beef, maple sugar, alcoholic beverages and processed foods. Israel won tariff concessions for selected fresh produce, processed foods and alcoholic beverages.
